newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police remove bodies from high-rise fire.
newsitem.headline: HK police remove bodies from high-rise fire.

text.p: Police on Friday began removing charred bodies from the scene of Hong Kong's worst building blaze in which at least 39 people died and scores of others were injured.

"We need to mark the location of the bodies; we need to take photographs of the bodies and then they will be put in bags and then taken to the mortuary for further investigation," said Dick Lee, assistant commissioner in charge of the police operation.

The inferno began on Wednesday in a 16-storey commercial building in a bustling tourist district of the territory and raged through the night, gutting seven floors. Some 300 firemen and 50 fire engines took almost 24 hours to quell the blaze.
Thirty-three bodies found at the site have yet to be identified, and another 39 people were reported missing.

Fire officials said sparks from welding in lift shafts was tentatively believed to be the cause of the blaze, Hong Kong's worst building fire in the past 100 years. They said they were still investigating the cause.
The closed design of the department store at the bottom of the Garley Building on Nathan Road, Kowloon, was believed to be a big factor in the fast spread of the fire.
Officials said 81 people were injured, 46 of whom were still in hospital. More than 110 people were rescued.
Lee said the police needed to carry out complicated examination procedures before relatives of the victims could identify the bodies.
A special unit of the police force -- the Disaster Victims Identification Unit -- had been sent to the mortuary, a police officer said.
